ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, A and C are at the two ends of the base; B is above; point E is located on the base AC, segment BE goes from vertex B through point Q to reach E; the figure also draws the other two medians intersecting at Q, and the problem gives that Q is centroid, BE=9. Reasoning: Because Q is the centroid of the triangle, the centroid is on each median, and divides the median in a 2:1 ratio in the direction from the vertex to the opposite side. Therefore on median BE, BQ:QE=2:1, so QE is one third of the whole BE. It is known that BE=9, so QE=9÷3=3.

Use the centroid theorem: a centroid lies on each median and divides the median in a 2:1 ratio, with the longer part adjacent to the vertex. Thus on median BE, BQ:QE=2:1, so QE is one third of BE: QE=9/3=3.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as triangle ABC with Q on cevian BE from vertex B to side AC. Since Q is the centroid, the line from B through Q meets AC at its midpoint E, so BE is a median. Set up coordinates along this median: place E at (0,0), let A=(-a,0), C=(a,0), and since BE=9 place B=(0,9). The centroid has coordinates equal to the average of the vertices: Q=((−a+0+a)/3,(0+9+0)/3)=(0,3). Therefore QE is the vertical distance from (0,0) to (0,3), so QE=3.
